newsitem.title: UK: Five hurt as security forces attacked in Belfast.
newsitem.headline: Five hurt as security forces attacked in Belfast.

text.p: Five members of the security forces were injured in Northern Ireland on Friday when a joint police and British army patrol came under fire in a republican area of Belfast, security sources said.
Ambulances were rushed to the scene and residents said two police officers and three soldiers had been hit in the late evening attack.
A police spokesman said: "We have got five casualties, both Royal Ulster Constabulary and military. It happened in a terrorist attack."
One resident said he heard about 20 shots fired at the patrol in the city's Ardoyne area, a Catholic nationalist stronghold.
There were also unconfirmed reports of an explosion, residents said.
Security forces have come under sniper attack in the past week during violence triggered by a Protestant march along the Catholic Garvaghy road area of Portadown, south of Belfast.
Hospital sources said that one of the casualties was a woman aged 30, who was wounded in the thigh and arm. She was said to be in stable condition.
The sources said three other casualties were taken to Musgrave Park, a military hospital in Belfast. Their condition, and that of the fifth casualty, was unknown.

Local media reported that earlier in the evening, leaflets purporting to come from a previously unheard-of group called the Cliftonville-Oldpark Defence Committee had been pushed through people's doors, telling them to stay off the streets.
The incident came as it appeared that tension had subsided after the Protestant Orange Order announced it was cancelling four flashpoint parades in Belfast and other towns.
